source_caption_text:
Nah 21 Savage was definitely making sure the mic worked before spittin verse 😭💀

21 Savage’s “a lot” is one of those songs that showed a completely different side of him. Released in 2018 as part of I Am > I Was, the track moves away from the usual hard-edged trap sound and gives 21 room to talk about everything he’s been through. The soulful sample in the background adds to that feeling, making the song sound reflective without losing the weight of his delivery.

21 keeps the verses personal, touching on loss, family, money, pressure, and the reality that comes with his lifestyle. Then J. Cole comes in with a long verse of his own, adding another perspective and giving the song even more depth. Their styles are different, but they work surprisingly well together, with both artists taking their time instead of rushing through the record.

The official video also gives the song another layer, showing a family gathering that looks perfect on the surface while revealing the struggles different people are dealing with underneath. That combination of the lyrics, production, visuals, and J. Cole’s feature helped turn “a lot” into much more than just another rap single. Even years later, it still feels like one of the most important songs from 21 Savage’s career.
